title: Company overview
text: Asterline Labs is a fictional workflow-monitoring software company. Its product, Asterline, collects workflow runs, helps teams investigate failures, and sends operational alerts. The company has offices in Pune and Dublin. This knowledge base is the only approved evidence source for this exercise.

title: Company overview
text: A workspace is a billing and access boundary. Projects belong to a workspace and each project has its own ingestion key. A workflow run contains a run_id, workflow_name, started_at, status, and optional attributes. A retry is a separate attempt associated with the same run_id.

title: Company overview
text: This overview is introductory, not a source for commercial limits or incident procedures. Use the dated pricing, product, policy, and operational documents for those questions. An employee or customer may describe their own workspace context; that statement does not establish a product-wide capability.

title: Plans and billing
text: Launch costs $59 per month and includes 4 seats and 1 million run records per month. Team costs $449 per month and includes 20 seats and 15 million run records per month. Enterprise pricing is negotiated; no list price is published. Annual billing gives a 12% discount on Launch and Team base subscriptions.

title: Plans and billing
text: Launch retains searchable run records for 21 days; Team for 180 days; Enterprise for 540 days. Run-record overage is $1.20 per 10,000 records on Launch and $0.70 per 10,000 on Team. Enterprise overage is negotiated. Extra Team seats cost $16 per seat per month; Launch cannot buy extra seats.

title: Plans and billing
text: Launch allows 6 alert rules per project, Team 75, and Enterprise 600. Warehouse Export is unavailable on Launch and included on Team and Enterprise. SAML SSO is Enterprise only. Team and Enterprise can create EU projects. Launch supports US projects only. A trial lasts 10 days with Team features and a total cap of 100,000 run records.

title: Service and support terms
text: Only Enterprise has a contractual monthly uptime SLA, set at 99.92%. Service credits are 10% below 99.92%, 25% below 99.5%, and 50% below 99.0%; the highest applicable tier applies, and credits are not added together.

title: Service and support terms
text: Launch receives email support within 2 business days. Team receives email and chat support within 6 business hours. Enterprise receives 24-hour support with a 45-minute response target for P1 cases. Response targets are not resolution promises.

title: Service and support terms
text: Planned maintenance announced at least 72 hours ahead is excluded from the uptime calculation. Customers must request service credits within 20 calendar days after the affected month ends. Trial workspaces do not have a contractual uptime SLA.

title: Run ingestion API
text: POST /v2/runs accepts at most 400 run records or 1 MB per request, whichever limit is reached first. A valid batch returns HTTP 202. Oversized requests return 413. Authentication uses a project ingestion key in the Authorization header; never paste actual keys into support conversations.

title: Run ingestion API
text: The per-project ingestion rate limit is 300 requests per second on Launch, 1500 on Team, and 6000 on Enterprise. A rate-limited request returns 429 and a Retry-After header. Clients should honor the header, use bounded retries, and retain stable event identifiers when retrying.

title: Run ingestion API
text: Duplicate submissions with the same event_id are suppressed for 48 hours. Records older than 96 hours are accepted with late=true. Each record supports at most 80 custom attributes and each attribute value is limited to 2 KB. Accepted records normally become searchable within 45 seconds; this is not a contractual guarantee.

title: Signals alert rules
text: Signals evaluate workflow metrics every 4 minutes. Supported modes are static threshold, percentage change against a previous period, and seasonal anomaly. Seasonal anomaly requires 21 complete days of history. Rules with insufficient history remain in a warming-up state.

title: Signals alert rules
text: Supported destinations are email, Slack, webhook, and PagerDuty. PagerDuty was added in version 2.3. Limits are 6 rules per project on Launch, 75 on Team, and 600 on Enterprise. A muted rule still evaluates but does not deliver notifications.

title: Signals alert rules
text: Since patch 2.3.1 the scheduler uses a monotonic clock and replays missed evaluation windows after recovery. This fixes the clock-adjustment defect in INC-2026-03. Replayed evaluations are tagged recovered=true so operators can distinguish delayed evaluations from live ones.

title: Warehouse Export specification
text: Warehouse Export sends selected run records to a customer warehouse. Team supports BigQuery and Snowflake. Enterprise supports BigQuery, Snowflake, and Redshift. Launch has no Warehouse Export. Redshift support began in version 2.2.

title: Warehouse Export specification
text: Exports can run as frequently as every 20 minutes. The destination receives an export_job_id and a record_hash. Since patch 2.1.2 the pair (export_job_id, record_hash) is the idempotency key; this replaced position-based deduplication after INC-2025-12.

title: Warehouse Export specification
text: Exports use a customer-managed warehouse credential stored in the secret vault. A failed job retries up to three times with backoff and then enters failed status. Operators can re-run failed jobs after resolving permissions. Deleting an Asterline record does not automatically delete copies already exported into the customer warehouse.

title: Run Explorer specification
text: Run Explorer shows the ordered attempts and status transitions for a workflow run. It is an operational timeline, not a recording of a user screen. Explorer is included on Team and Enterprise and is unavailable on Launch.

title: Run Explorer specification
text: Explorer timeline retention is 14 days on Team and 60 days on Enterprise. This is separate from searchable run-record retention. Sampling is 50% on Team and 100% on Enterprise, selected deterministically by run_id.

title: Run Explorer specification
text: Users can filter timelines by workflow name, status, environment, and custom attributes. A shareable timeline link requires workspace access and does not grant anonymous viewing. Deleting a project removes its timeline access immediately.

title: AQL query reference
text: AQL is a read-only query language. Example: RUNS WHERE status = failed SINCE 7d COUNT BY workflow_name. Queries return at most 8000 rows and time out after 50 seconds in version 2.3. Earlier versions used a 25-second timeout.

title: AQL query reference
text: Per-workspace query concurrency is 6 on Launch, 30 on Team, and 120 on Enterprise. Queries beyond this limit are rejected with 429. Ingestion limits are per project and must not be confused with these workspace query limits.

title: AQL query reference
text: Queries read the hot store for the most recent 5 days and object storage for older data. Results are cached for 8 minutes. An explicit bypass_cache option is available to workspace admins; it does not increase query limits or retention.

title: SDK integration guide
text: Official SDKs are available for JavaScript, Python, Java, and Go. The JavaScript SDK supports Node.js services. SDKs submit workflow lifecycle events and are not browser session-recording libraries.

title: SDK integration guide
text: SDKs flush a batch every 15 seconds or when it reaches 100 records. On retry they retain the original event_id. Buffer capacity is 5000 records per process by default; when full, the oldest unsent record is dropped and a warning is logged.

title: SDK integration guide
text: Version 2.2 introduced an async Python client. Applications must call flush during graceful shutdown and allow up to 10 seconds for completion. Use separate project keys for development and production. Keys are configured through environment variables.

title: Regions and workspace setup
text: Asterline has a US region in Virginia and an EU region in Dublin. US is the default. EU projects are available on Team and Enterprise starting with version 2.1. Launch workspaces can create only US projects.

title: Regions and workspace setup
text: Region is selected when a project is created and cannot be changed in place. To move future ingestion, create a project in the target region and update SDK credentials and endpoints. Existing historical records are not transferred by this procedure.

title: Regions and workspace setup
text: A workspace may contain projects in both supported regions if its plan permits EU projects. Queries and alert rules operate within a project region. No launch date has been announced for an Asia-Pacific region.

title: Version 2.0 release notes
text: Version 2.0 shipped on 2025-08-12. It introduced the Queuefin ingestion pipeline and Run Explorer for Team and Enterprise. Launch ingestion was limited to 180 requests per second per project at this release.

title: Version 2.0 release notes
text: Patch 2.0.1 shipped on 2025-08-22 and fixed the consumer configuration mismatch responsible for INC-2025-08. The rollout now checks consumer heartbeat configuration before advancing to production.

title: Version 2.0 release notes
text: Version 2.0 retained a 25-second AQL query timeout. It supported email, Slack, and webhook alert destinations. EU projects, Redshift export, and PagerDuty were not introduced in this release.

title: Version 2.1 release notes
text: Version 2.1 shipped on 2025-11-18. It introduced EU projects in Dublin for Team and Enterprise and seasonal anomaly alerting. Launch ingestion increased from 180 to 300 requests per second per project. Other plan ingestion limits stayed unchanged.

title: Version 2.1 release notes
text: Version 2.1 replaced the query engine with Heron. The new engine changed export row ordering, exposing a flaw in position-based deduplication. INC-2025-12 documents the resulting duplicate warehouse rows.

title: Version 2.1 release notes
text: Patch 2.1.2 shipped on 2025-12-08. It changed Warehouse Export deduplication to (export_job_id, record_hash), resolving INC-2025-12. A cleanup script was provided to affected customers; merely upgrading did not remove existing duplicate rows.

title: Version 2.2 release notes
text: Version 2.2 shipped on 2026-02-05. It added Redshift Warehouse Export for Enterprise and the async Python SDK. Team warehouse destinations remained BigQuery and Snowflake.

title: Version 2.2 release notes
text: The release added environment filtering in Run Explorer. It did not change Explorer sampling or retention. Enterprise timelines remained available for 60 days and Team timelines for 14 days.

title: Version 2.2 release notes
text: Version 2.2 retained the 25-second AQL timeout. It did not add an Asia-Pacific region or alter the restriction against changing a project region in place.

title: Version 2.3 release notes
text: Version 2.3 shipped on 2026-03-03. It added PagerDuty as a Signals destination and increased the AQL timeout from 25 to 50 seconds. Query row limits and concurrency limits were unchanged.

title: Version 2.3 release notes
text: Patch 2.3.1 shipped on 2026-03-10. It fixed the clock-adjustment defect in INC-2026-03 using a monotonic scheduler clock and replay of missed evaluation windows. No alerts were lost during the incident.

title: Version 2.3 release notes
text: Customers using the managed service receive scheduler fixes automatically. SDK upgrades are not required to receive the 2.3.1 scheduler fix. This release did not change plan prices, run-record retention, or support response targets.

title: Ingestion and query architecture
text: The ingestion path is API gateway, Go ingestion workers, Kafka topic runs.raw, enrichers, Kafka topic runs.enriched, and storage writers. Both Kafka topics have 72 partitions. Raw payloads are validated before entering runs.raw.

title: Ingestion and query architecture
text: Writers store recent data in ClickHouse and longer-lived records as Parquet in object storage. The hot-store window is 5 days. The Heron query engine routes reads based on the requested time range and merges results when a query crosses that boundary.

title: Ingestion and query architecture
text: Query results have an 8-minute cache TTL. Kafka offsets track ingestion progress and are independent of client event_id deduplication. A successful HTTP 202 acknowledges acceptance, not completion of all downstream writes.

title: Deployment runbook
text: Production deployments use blue/green releases with canary stages at 10%, 40%, and 100%. Each stage has a 15-minute observation period. Operators record the release version and deployment identifier before starting.

title: Deployment runbook
text: Roll back automatically if the error rate exceeds 0.8% or p95 latency exceeds 900 milliseconds during a canary stage. The deployment controller also validates Kafka consumer heartbeat settings after INC-2025-08.

title: Deployment runbook
text: A rollback restores application binaries and configuration, but does not remove warehouse rows already exported. Data cleanup requires the incident-specific procedure. The incident commander decides when to resume a halted rollout.

title: On-call runbook
text: The primary and secondary on-call engineers rotate weekly. This runbook lists an on-call stipend of $140 per week. The engineering manager maintains the rota and publishes handover notes on Fridays.

title: On-call runbook
text: SEV-1 is a customer-facing outage: page immediately and publish a status update within 10 minutes. SEV-2 is degraded service: publish an update within 45 minutes. SEV-3 is a minor issue: update on the next business day.

title: On-call runbook
text: The primary engineer becomes incident commander until relieved. The secondary maintains a timeline and gathers evidence. A post-mortem must record impact, cause, recovery, and follow-up actions without exposing customer secrets.

title: INC-2025-08 ingestion outage
text: INC-2025-08 occurred on 2025-08-20 from 08:10 to 10:40 UTC, lasting 2 hours 30 minutes. Approximately 32% of US ingestion requests returned 503. The incident was SEV-1.

title: INC-2025-08 ingestion outage
text: The cause was a consumer heartbeat configuration mismatch introduced during the Queuefin rollout. Rebalances repeatedly interrupted ingestion workers. SDK clients that retried recovered; clients without retry lost approximately 1.4 million records.

title: INC-2025-08 ingestion outage
text: Patch 2.0.1 fixed the mismatch. Deployment validation now checks heartbeat settings before a canary advances. This incident concerned ingestion availability, not Warehouse Export duplication.

title: INC-2025-12 duplicate exports
text: INC-2025-12 affected 29 Team and Enterprise customers using BigQuery or Snowflake between 2025-12-04 and 2025-12-07. Warehouse Export wrote duplicate rows. It was a SEV-2 incident.

title: INC-2025-12 duplicate exports
text: Heron changed query result ordering, which broke position-based export deduplication. The fix replaced row position with the stable pair (export_job_id, record_hash). The fix shipped in patch 2.1.2.

title: INC-2025-12 duplicate exports
text: Affected customers received a cleanup script for pre-existing duplicates. The fix prevented new duplicates but did not itself delete old ones. Redshift customers were not affected because that destination had not yet launched.

title: INC-2026-03 delayed alerts
text: INC-2026-03 occurred on 2026-03-07 from 16:05 to 16:39 UTC. Signals notifications were delayed by up to 34 minutes. No alerts were lost. The incident was classified SEV-3.

title: INC-2026-03 delayed alerts
text: A time synchronization configuration change moved scheduler wall clocks backward. The scheduler incorrectly skipped evaluation windows. Patch 2.3.1 introduced a monotonic clock and replay of missed windows.

title: INC-2026-03 delayed alerts
text: Time synchronization configuration is now managed through reviewed infrastructure changes. The incident did not change the normal 4-minute evaluation interval or the 21-day seasonal anomaly history requirement.

title: Data retention policy
text: Effective 2026-01-15, raw run records are held in cold recovery storage for 20 days after their plan-specific searchable retention period ends, then permanently deleted. This policy supersedes the earlier 60-day cold-storage period.

title: Data retention policy
text: Deleted-account data is purged within 10 days. Backups are retained for 28 days. Cold recovery storage is not normally searchable through AQL, so it must not be added to the advertised searchable retention window.

title: Data retention policy
text: These rules cover Asterline-managed storage. Copies exported to a customer warehouse are controlled by that customer. Run Explorer timeline retention is specified separately and is not extended by cold recovery storage.

title: Security overview
text: Asterline encrypts data with AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2 or later in transit. Project ingestion keys can be rotated by workspace admins. SAML SSO is available only on Enterprise.

title: Security overview
text: This overview states that raw run records remain in cold recovery storage for 60 days after searchable retention ends. It was published on 2025-03-15 and has not been revised since publication.

title: Security overview
text: Annual penetration testing is performed by Northbridge Security. Security reports should omit tokens, credentials, and customer payloads unless a secure transfer is arranged. This overview makes no claims about healthcare-specific certifications.

title: Employee handbook
text: Employees receive 22 days of annual leave and 10 days of sick leave each year. Hybrid teams attend the office on Wednesdays and Thursdays. Managers approve exceptions based on team needs.

title: Employee handbook
text: Effective 2026-01-01 the weekly on-call stipend is $175, replacing $140. This compensation update supersedes stipend figures in older operational runbooks. Incident severity definitions remain owned by the on-call runbook.

title: Employee handbook
text: Primary parental leave is 24 weeks and secondary parental leave is 6 weeks. Employees should use the HR portal for personal leave requests rather than adding private medical details to shared operational notes.

title: Customer onboarding guide
text: Start by choosing a workspace plan and creating a project in the required supported region. Configure a project ingestion key through the application environment and send one test workflow run. Verify visibility before enabling full-volume ingestion.

title: Customer onboarding guide
text: Create a threshold Signal first; seasonal anomaly requires 21 complete days of history. For Team and Enterprise, configure Warehouse Export only after the customer grants the required warehouse permissions. Test a small export before enabling the regular schedule.

title: Customer onboarding guide
text: Check searchable record retention and Run Explorer retention separately. For a region move, create a new project and redirect future ingestion; historical records are not migrated automatically. The current pricing and region documents govern eligibility.

title: Product FAQ
text: Asterline is a workflow-monitoring service. Run Explorer displays workflow attempts and status changes; it does not capture screens or DOM content. Signals notifications can be delayed during incidents even when the underlying run records remain available.

title: Product FAQ
text: There is no announced timeline for an Asia-Pacific region. No mobile dashboard application is planned for 2026. Enterprise subscription prices must be obtained from sales and are not published in this knowledge base.

title: Product FAQ
text: When documentation differs, compare the specific topic, effective date, scope, and explicit supersession statement. A later general overview does not automatically override a specific policy. Ask for clarification when the evidence cannot resolve a disagreement.
